text:
tess: quick flag  canary for a newly onboarded model 'ceres-bridgeq' (int8) shows a jump in structured output parse errors on our toolcall bench. went from ~0.5% to ~5.4% starting at 07:42 UTC.
vik: what slice + config?
tess: bench-ci ran 4k-toolcall-v2 (slice-id: 2026-03-25-e). config: model=ceres-bridgeq, quant=int8, batch_size=12, kv_prefix=true, streaming=true, kernel=attn_fused.
bench-ci: run summary:
```
job: bc-1738
samples: 4000
parse_failure_rate: 0.054
failure_modes: trailing-data, missing-comma-between-objects, unescaped-control
```
hao: can you paste a sanitized failing snippet? even one example helps triage.
tess: pasted example (sanitized):
```
{"action":"call","name":"lookup","arguments":{"id":"q-77"}}}{"action":"call","name":"lookup","arguments":{"id":"q-78"}}
```
vik: extra brace then another object appended. smells like suffix duplication from streaming stitch or prefix replay. any recent infra/decoder changes?
tess: this canary included both the int8 quant profile and a new attention kernel. earlier int16+old-kernel run had parse_fail 0.8%.
parse-bot: auto-observation: 71% of failures contain one of these patterns: trailing '}' plus appended JSON, adjacent objects inside arrays without commas, or strings with raw newlines.
hao: triage plan: 1) quick matrix: kv_prefix on/off, streaming on/off, batch sizes 1/8/32 2) run int16 with new kernel to separate quant vs kernel 3) add temporary SDK repair heuristics: (A) trailing-trim (drop anything after last '}' up to 128 chars), (B) ndjson-insert (insert commas between '}{' in arrays), (C) escape-sanitizer (escape control chars). tag repaired calls with header `x-ceres-repaired` and metric `ceres_repair_type`.
tess: agreed. also block promotion pipeline for ceres-bridgeq-int8 until we stabilize. i'll set routing hold.
bench-ci: queued quick jobs: bc-1739 (kv_prefix=false, limit=1000), bc-1740 (streaming=false, limit=1000), bc-1741 (int16+new-kernel, limit=1000).
bench-ci: interim bc-1739: kv_prefix=false -> parse_fail dropped to 0.012 in 1k sample run. strong signal kv_prefix playback is amplifying problem.
vik: that's useful. sounds like kv_prefix replay interacts badly with int8 token probabilities at chunk boundaries.
hao: next step: run with repairs enabled + kv_prefix=false on full 4k slice to measure repaired_success vs false positives. also collect token logits for a sample of fails (50).
bench-ci: queued bc-1742: full 4k repairs=on, kv_prefix=false (job link: https://bench.internal/runs/bc-1742).
parse-bot: automated note: canary parse failure > 5% for 10m  routing hold placed; no escalation.
tess: also add unit test to canary harness that simulates streaming-chunk boundary with punctuation tokens split across frames. we should catch this before onboarding next time.
bench-ci: bc-1742 finished: repaired_success_rate=0.058; final parse_fail reduced to 0.010; false_repair_est=0.002 on gold subset. logs: https://bench.internal/runs/bc-1742/logs
vik: good. temporary mitigations: A) keep routing block for 24h B) runtime change: disallow kv_prefix replay for quant=int8 by default C) ship SDK repair heuristics for canary only with telemetry D) ingest all minimal failing cases into s3://eng-ml/goldens/ceres-bridgeq/ for model team.
hao: will implement gating for kv_prefix+int8 and emit `kv_prefix_blocked` metric. i'll also ensure token logits are captured for the 50 sampled failures and uploaded.
tess: ash? (not in thread) can you coordinate with docs/SDK to surface the repair header and how customers are notified?
vik: follow-ups: run a matrix of stream true/false x batch 1/8/32 with int8+kv_prefix off to see residual fragility; schedule a model-owner sync to discuss retraining/tokenizer fixes.
bench-ci: additional note: repairs fixed ~5.8% of previously failing calls but introduced an estimated false_repair rate of ~0.2% relative to gold. acceptable for canary, but we'll be conservative for prod.
parse-bot: incident ticket INC-1738 created and linked to bc-1742.
tess: summary (owners): tess -> routing hold + product note, hao -> runtime kv_prefix gating + metrics + logits collection, vik -> regression dashboard + matrix runs, bench-ci -> keep gold set + reruns, parse-bot -> incident tracking.
vik: thanks team. please dump minimal failing traces into the goldens bucket and we'll reconvene once the matrix finishes. :thumbsup:
tess: closing when dashboard shows stable <1% parse_fail for 24h.
